adopted: default exhaustive maps (finite source in binary64 integer range, no bounds, no screen, template height <= 65536) use exhaustiveNcc: uint32 column sums slid vertically and uint64 window sums slid horizontally replace the binary64 integral images

UDOT builds (Backend::Auto, template width <= 4096) compute products of eight adjacent windows per kernel call over a zero-padded template and a tight zero-tailed source copy; groups whose eight denominators are all zero are skipped like the original per-window skip
bounded and screened maps keep the original code path unchanged

rejected_in_pilot.variant: pilot 1: four-row interleaved whole-window UDOT + uint64 integral images
rejected_in_pilot.reason: Src7/Src6 only -11%: level-0 templates exceed L1, so every window re-streamed the template; the integral images still wrote 16 bytes per ROI pixel
about 2x slower than row-by-row on wide templates (one long dependency chain)

failures_and_caveats: two early profiling attempts were invalid (duplicated dot calls merged by the compiler; a patch that did not apply); both are disclosed in pilot/pilot-console-transcript.txt and superseded
pilot timings were printed to the console only; they are transcribed verbatim in pilot/pilot-console-transcript.txt; the window microbenchmark was rerun once to archive its output
the grouped kernel reads up to 22 bytes past a window inside a private zero-tailed copy; mutant N6 (no tail) is caught only by ASan
Backend::Scalar also changes how window sums are formed (exact integer sliding sums), so portable_scalar mode is faster (-11.6%); its dot product is unchanged
the integer code is platform independent; x86 was not run
other Claude/Codex processes were active; load averages recorded per session (1-minute 3.7-4.4)
